questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been pretty determined to study abroad in America, and crucial aspects to choosing the exact destination were definitely the courses offered and the accessibility to information about international students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival everything was very easy for me. I had gotten all of the information in emails weeks before arriving. I also knew who to contact if I needed additional assistance or info.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some help with an immigration practicality.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of dorms and the Global LLC, which is where I live, welcome students from all over the world.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Living on campus there is an obligatory meal plan for unlimited food at the dining halls. There are also small community kitchens at most of the dorms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When you live on campus here, you are obligated to pay for the unlimited meal plan. You pay this in your housing payment, which also includes 300 dollars towards a "student account" which you can only use at campus facilities. This really means that you are forced to spend 300 dollars on campus facilities, because you can't get the money back.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For international students, housing availability could be better in my opinion. There are very limited spots, and most internationals live off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to know the unique number for every course to register for them. The system in which you do it, seems a little old fashioned, but it works. You put in the unique number and add yourself to the courses individually. You are provided with a certain time slot with access to the registration website, and you need to add the courses fast, because a lot of other people are doing it at the same time. It works on a first come first served basis. If you don't get into the classes you want, you can add yourself to a waitlist and see if room becomes available.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutorials on how to use the course registration website were provided and we also went over it during an orientation for international students over zoom.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to register for 4 courses but I tried to get into 5 so that I could try them all before dropping 1. However, there was one class that was full when I tried to register for it, so I put myself on the waiting list. The next day I got lucky and got an email saying that I got in. I ended up will all of the classes I hoped for and got to drop one that I didn't like.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend time making a good plan for the class schedule you want and then be ready with the unique numbers when its your time slot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One of my classes was upper division and the level here was higher and more was expected of you. I would compare this upper level class to the ones that I've had at UCPH. My other classes were not very hard to get good results in - coming from a student with 2 years of university experience of course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much was the same. One of my classes was only online lectures, one was in-person lectures and labs, and my other two classes were smaller in-person classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Biological anthropology
2. Introduction to psychology
3. Shakespeare
4. Women, gender, literature, culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them. I really enjoyed them because they are very different from each other, and I got to explore new interests.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Being forced to set money aside to use at on-campus facilities

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think housing and insurance were more expensive than I expected. Housing is expensive because it includes the meal plan, but still a lot of money pr. month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A LOT of student organizations and clubs are available for all sorts of culture, interests, sports, etc. There is also museums on campus as well an a giant gym, shopping facilities, and coffee shops.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting out and exploring the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to museums, go shopping, go outside of campus, go to sports games.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy. Very few differences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The locals are extremely open here, and if you just push yourself a little and get out there, it is easy to get a friend group.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The education system and the expectation to get good grades in everything is different from home. I could see this affecting mostly local students, but some internationals might get sucked into the performance culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I mostly appreciated the openness of the locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take fun courses that aren't available at home, prioritize going to games and experiencing the school spirit, remember to have fun outside of campus and enjoy that you get to study in and experience another culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is always help if you need it, and though the process for all the practical stuff you need to do before going is hard, you can do it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My new friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge during the exchange had more to do with my home university. There is not really any communication and most of the time you are left to figure everything out yourself. My challenge was to plan my next semester at home while help was hard to get, and no one reminded me to do anything. I mean in regards to registering for courses and finding an advisor for my BA project, etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
